items.title: Jesus Ascends to Heaven
items.description: After his resurrection Jesus gives final instructions and ascends to heaven. The apostles return to Jerusalem and choose Matthias to replace Judas.

items.title: The Spirit Descends at Pentecost
items.description: The Holy Spirit fills the believers at Pentecost and they speak in other tongues. Peter preaches to the crowd, and three thousand are added to the church.

items.title: Peter Heals the Lame Man at the Gate
items.description: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth at the temple gate. Peter proclaims that faith in the name of Jesus has made the man completely well.

items.title: Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
items.description: Peter and John are arrested and questioned by the rulers, but boldly testify about Jesus. The believers pray for courage and share everything they own.

items.title: Ananias and Sapphira; Apostles Beaten
items.description: Ananias and Sapphira fall dead for lying to the Holy Spirit. The apostles heal many, are jailed and flogged, yet keep preaching Christ without fear.

items.title: Seven Servants Chosen; Stephen Arrested
items.description: Seven men, including Stephen, are chosen to serve the widows. Stephen works great wonders but is seized on false charges and brought before the Sanhedrin.

items.title: Stephen's Sermon and Martyrdom
items.description: Stephen recounts Israel's history and rebukes his accusers. Seeing heaven opened, he is stoned to death as the first martyr, forgiving his killers.

items.title: Philip in Samaria; the Ethiopian Eunuch
items.description: Persecution scatters the church. Philip preaches in Samaria, confronts Simon the sorcerer, and leads an Ethiopian official to faith and baptism.

items.title: Saul's Conversion on the Road to Damascus
items.description: The risen Jesus confronts Saul on the road to Damascus. Blinded and then healed, Saul is baptized and begins to preach that Jesus is the Son of God.

items.title: Cornelius and Peter; Gospel to Gentiles
items.description: Guided by visions, Peter visits the Roman centurion Cornelius. The Holy Spirit falls on the Gentiles, and they too are baptized as believers.

items.title: Peter Explains; First Called Christians
items.description: Peter defends welcoming the Gentiles. The gospel spreads to Antioch, where the disciples are first called Christians and send famine relief to Judea.

items.title: Peter Freed from Prison; Herod Dies
items.description: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but an angel frees him during the night. Herod is later struck down, and the word of God continues to spread.

items.title: Paul's First Missionary Journey Begins
items.description: The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul. Sailing to Cyprus and Antioch, Paul preaches that forgiveness comes through Jesus, dividing his hearers.

items.title: Paul Stoned at Lystra; Returns to Antioch
items.description: In Lystra Paul heals a lame man and is mistaken for a god, then stoned. He and Barnabas strengthen the young churches and return to Antioch.

items.title: The Jerusalem Council Settles a Debate
items.description: The apostles and elders meet in Jerusalem and decide Gentiles need not keep the law of Moses. Paul and Barnabas then part company over John Mark.

items.title: The Macedonian Call; Philippian Jailer
items.description: Called to Macedonia, Paul converts Lydia and casts out a spirit. Jailed in Philippi, an earthquake frees him and leads the jailer to faith.

items.title: Paul on Mars Hill in Athens
items.description: Paul preaches in Thessalonica and Berea, then in Athens proclaims the 'unknown god' to the philosophers gathered on the Areopagus.

items.title: Paul in Corinth; Apollos Taught
items.description: Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth and is brought before Gallio. Apollos is taught the way of God more accurately at Ephesus.

items.title: Paul in Ephesus; Riot of Silversmiths
items.description: In Ephesus Paul performs great miracles and many burn their scrolls, until silversmiths who profit from idols stir up a riot in the theater.

items.title: Eutychus Raised; Farewell at Miletus
items.description: Paul raises Eutychus, who fell from a window during his sermon. At Miletus he gives a moving farewell to the Ephesian elders, bound for Jerusalem.

items.title: Paul is Arrested at the Temple
items.description: Despite repeated warnings, Paul goes to Jerusalem. A mob seizes him in the temple, and Roman soldiers arrest him to save his life from the crowd.

items.title: Paul Defends Himself Before the Crowd
items.description: Paul addresses the crowd and recounts his conversion. When he mentions the Gentiles they erupt in fury, and he reveals his Roman citizenship.

items.title: Plot Against Paul; Sent to Caesarea
items.description: Paul divides the Sanhedrin over the resurrection. When forty men vow to kill him, the commander sends him under heavy guard to Caesarea.

items.title: Paul Pleads His Case Before Felix
items.description: Accused before Governor Felix, Paul defends his faith and his hope in the resurrection. Felix leaves him imprisoned, hoping for a bribe.

items.title: Paul Appeals to Caesar Before Festus
items.description: Festus succeeds Felix. Facing his accusers again, Paul appeals to Caesar, and Festus consults King Agrippa about how to handle the case.

items.title: Paul's Defense Before King Agrippa
items.description: Paul tells King Agrippa his story of conversion and calling. Agrippa admits that Paul has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment.

items.title: Storm and Shipwreck on the Way to Rome
items.description: Sailing for Rome as a prisoner, Paul endures a violent storm. The ship is wrecked off Malta, yet everyone aboard reaches land safely as he foretold.

items.title: Paul Reaches Rome and Preaches Boldly
items.description: On Malta Paul survives a snakebite and heals the sick. Arriving at last in Rome, he preaches the kingdom of God boldly and without hindrance.

original.title: The Visual Bible: Acts
original.film_description: The Acts of the Apostles is the New Testament account of the birth and rapid growth of the early Church. Written by Luke as a sequel to his Gospel, Acts traces the outpouring of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost, the bold witness of Peter and the apostles, the conversion of Saul into the apostle Paul, and the spread of the gospel from Jerusalem through Judea and Samaria to the ends of the earth. It shows how the message of Jesus crossed every cultural and political boundary to reach Rome itself.
original.shortDescription: The complete Book of Acts dramatized word-for-word from the NIV, with Dean Jones narrating as Luke, James Brolin as Peter, and Bruce Marchiano reprising his role as Jesus.

It shows how the message of Jesus crossed every cultural and political boundary to reach Rome itself.

items.title: Ezra Enters Jerusalem
items.description: The opening frame narrative. The priest-scribe Ezra returns to Jerusalem and prepares to recount the foundational story of God's covenant with Israel — setting the stage for the great Torah retelling that follows.

items.title: The Creation of Humanity
items.description: God creates the heavens and the earth, forms Adam and Eve in His image, and places them in the garden. The first humans break trust with their Creator and are cast out into a world marked by hardship — the entry point of every story that follows.

items.title: Noah, the Flood and the Next Generation
items.description: As violence fills the earth, God grieves and resolves to begin again. Noah finds favor and builds the ark. The flood comes and recedes, and God establishes His covenant with Noah, setting the rainbow in the sky as a sign for every generation.

items.title: The Lord's Covenant with Abraham
items.description: God calls Abram out of his homeland and promises to make him a great nation through whom all peoples will be blessed. In a vision and through the sign of circumcision, God formalizes His covenant with Abraham and his descendants.

items.title: The Birth of Isaac
items.description: Long after Abraham and Sarah have given up hope of children, the Lord visits them and reaffirms His promise. Sarah laughs, but in the appointed time Isaac — the child of promise — is born.

items.title: Abraham Tested
items.description: God tests Abraham's faith by commanding him to offer his only son Isaac on Mount Moriah. As Abraham raises the knife, the Lord intervenes, providing a ram in Isaac's place — a defining picture of trust, sacrifice, and God's provision.

items.title: Joseph's Dream
items.description: Jacob's favored son Joseph dreams that his family will one day bow before him. His brothers' jealousy boils over, and they sell him into slavery in Egypt — beginning a long providential journey that will preserve the family of promise.

items.title: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
items.description: In Egypt, Joseph rises to a place of trust in the household of Potiphar. Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife after refusing her advances, he is thrown into prison — yet the Lord remains with him.

items.title: Joseph's Brothers Go to Egypt
items.description: Years later, Joseph has risen to become governor of Egypt. When famine drives his brothers down from Canaan in search of grain, they unknowingly come before the brother they betrayed. Joseph reveals himself, forgives them, and the family of Israel is reunited and resettled in Egypt.

items.title: The Israelites Oppressed
items.description: Generations later a new pharaoh arises who does not remember Joseph. The Hebrews multiply and are forced into bitter slavery. Among them a Hebrew boy named Moses is hidden in the reeds and grows up in Pharaoh's own household.

items.title: Moses and the Burning Bush
items.description: After fleeing Egypt, Moses keeps flocks in Midian. On Mount Horeb the Lord appears in a bush that burns without being consumed and commissions Moses to return to Egypt and bring His people out of slavery.

items.title: The Passover, the Exodus, and the Covenant at Sinai
items.description: Moses confronts Pharaoh, the plagues fall on Egypt, and the Passover lamb is slain. Israel is freed and crosses the Red Sea on dry ground. In the wilderness God provides manna and quail, gives the Ten Commandments at Sinai, and renews His covenant with His people — calling them to choose life and the promised land that lies ahead.

original.book_description: The Covenant is Lumo Project Films' visually captivating, word-for-word adaptation of the Torah — the first five books of the Bible. Framed by the prophet-priest Ezra returning to Jerusalem and recounting the foundational story of Israel, the film traces the great Old Testament arc from the creation of humanity through the patriarchs Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph, on to Moses, the Exodus from Egypt, and the giving of the law at Sinai. Available in 37+ languages, it is designed for church and television audiences as a faithful, biblically-literate bridge to understanding the God who keeps His promises.
